newsitem.title: UKRAINE: MINISTER SAYS IMF CLOSER TO AGREEING UKRAINE LOAN.
newsitem.headline: MINISTER SAYS IMF CLOSER TO AGREEING UKRAINE LOAN.

text.p: Economy Minister Vasyl Hureyev said on Wednesday Ukrainian officials and an International Monetary Fund mission had agreed most of a deal paving the way for a multi-billion dollar loan programme which would start in 1997.
"We have agreed on about 80 percent of our memorandum with the IMF, and only about 20 percent remains to be done," Hureyev told Reuters.
The IMF mission, in Kiev to negotiate a $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and review the next tranche of an $867 million stand-by credit, would leave on November 14.
Hureyev said talks had proceeded normally and that the mission supported Ukraine's proposals for tax reform next year.
But a sticking point was the planned budget deficit and how to cover it, he said.

Ukraine had planned a deficit at 3.8 percent, or three percent by Western calculations, but a presidential aide said on Wednesday that the government would ask parliament to increase the deficit to 5.8 percent or four percent by Western standards.
"Confirmation of the 1997 budget by January 1 is also a principal issue for the IMF," Hureyev said, adding that solving it would "open the doors to the EFF credit."
Ukraine's new constitution also states that the annual budget, to go before parliament for approval at the end of the month, must be passed by the start of the year.
The EFF would succeed the stand-by programme agreed in May.
